tier_reason: First-party README plots (performance/RTX3090/*.png, y-axis in TFLOPS) from the public harness benchmarks/python/benchmark_decoding_attn.py, which times flash_attn_with_kvcache (FlashAttention v2.6.3) and FlashInfer v0.1.6 alongside the project's kernel with CUDA events. GPU and CUDA 12.1 are stated, and nvcc flags are in CMakeLists.txt (-O3 --use_fast_math), but the host CPU and host compiler are not, so it is C, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README text: faster than Flash-Decoding and FlashInfer below sequence length 1536 (batch 1), slower above it, and faster than both at every batch size with sequence length 128. Approximate plot readings (derived from page data), RTX 3090 FP16 MHA, 32 heads, head dim 128: batch sweep at seq 128, about 0.69 TFLOPS vs FlashInfer 0.50 and Flash-Decoding 0.42 at batch 16 (about 1.4x and 1.6x); at batch 128 and above about 0.86 vs 0.85 and 0.55 (about 1.0x and 1.55x). Sequence sweep at batch 1: about 1.75x both baselines at seq 1024 (0.34 vs 0.19 TFLOPS), but at seq 8192 FlashInfer reaches about 0.84 TFLOPS against 0.43, so the project is about 2x slower there. MLA on H20 (README plots, no other baseline): FlashMLA is faster everywhere, about 12x at batch 1 to about 70x at batch 128 and above in the batch sweep (seq 4096; FlashMLA 41 to 127 TFLOPS vs about 1.7 to 3.4), and 1.3x at seq 256 to about 18x at seq 8192 in the batch-1 sequence sweep.
corrections.caveats: Single-developer repository with two commits; results are plots only (the RTX 3090 plots label the TFLOPS axis only at 0 and 1). The win is limited to short contexts: FlashInfer and Flash-Decoding win above sequence length 1536, and on the H20 MLA plots FlashMLA is 1.3x to about 70x faster than this project. The FlashInfer baseline is the author's fork (Bruce-Lee-LY/flashinfer, v0.1.6), and the harness times only 1 warmup and 10 iterations. Host CPU and host compiler are not stated. Baselines are FlashAttention-family kernels, not cuDNN.

notes: Metadata confirmed on the GitHub page: BSD-3-Clause, 48 stars, 4 forks, 2 commits (latest 2025-06-11, 'support mla'), not archived or a fork; stale. Shortcoming to record: the MLA comparison the README plots shows the project far slower than FlashMLA, and the FlashInfer baseline is the author's own fork.

tier_reason: First-party NVIDIA README figures and docs/bert_guide.md latency tables against TensorFlow XLA and TorchScript on a T4 with an Intel Xeon E5-2670 host, produced by public scripts (benchmarks/bert/tf_benchmark.sh, pyt_benchmark.sh, benchmarks/decoding/*.sh). CMakeLists.txt holds the Release flags, but the compiler and CUDA version used for the measurements are not stated, so it is C, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (T4, FP16 baselines): BERT base vs TensorFlow XLA about 3x for small batch and sequence, about 5x for large ones with Effective FasterTransformer plus INT8-v2; vs PyTorch TorchScript 4x to 6x small, about 5x large. Translation decoding vs TensorFlow: FT-Decoder 1.5x to 3x, FT-Decoding 4x to 18x; vs PyTorch: 1.2x to 3x and 3.8x to 13x. docs/bert_guide.md T4 tables: same-precision FP16 FT vs TF XLA 1.28x to 3.04x (EFF-FT 1.33x to 3.29x); FP16 FT vs TorchScript 1.52x to 6.41x (EFF-FT 2.44x to 3.78x); EFF-FT INT8-v2 vs TF-FP16 up to 5.53x (batch 8, seq 384: 39.50 ms vs 7.14 ms).
corrections.baseline: TensorFlow XLA (FP16) and PyTorch TorchScript (FP16) for the BERT encoder; TensorFlow and PyTorch decoder and beam-search implementations for translation decoding
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the measurements; CMakeLists.txt Release build uses -O3 for C++ and -Xcompiler -O3 --use_fast_math for CUDA, and the guide recommends the NGC tensorflow:22.09-tf1-py3 / pytorch:22.09-py3 containers
corrections.caveats: First-party NVIDIA numbers. The '5x' headlines compare INT8 FasterTransformer against FP16 framework baselines; same-precision FP16 FT vs TF XLA on T4 is 1.28x to 3.04x. The TorchScript FP16 baseline stays near 10.4 to 11 ms for all small cases (overhead-bound), which inflates the 4x to 6x small-batch ratios. Compiler and CUDA version for the runs are not stated. Baselines are framework implementations of the era, not cuDNN. NVIDIA states the repo will see no further development (moved to TensorRT-LLM). Third-party tables (ByteTransformer, CTranslate2 READMEs) show newer kernels beating it in several settings.

notes: Metadata confirmed on the GitHub page: Apache-2.0, 6.5k stars, 935 forks, not archived or a fork, last commit 2023-10-19 (README update); release 5.2 (Dec 2022). Stale by date and will pass 3 years in October 2026; the README's discontinuation notice could justify abandoned.

tier_reason: The first-party wiki gives inference-time tables against Caffe+OpenBLAS, Caffe2+Eigen, Caffe2+NNPACK, TensorFlow Lite and ACL on named ARM devices, but it links no benchmark code and states no compiler or flags, so it is C. The README cites a peer-reviewed IEEE TPDS paper (DOI 10.1109/TPDS.2019.2939785) that may justify B, but every host serving it was blocked here and it could not be opened.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Wiki, Huawei D05 (64 Cortex-A72 cores), best time at any thread count: VGG-16 102 ms vs Caffe+OpenBLAS 1108 ms (10.86x) and Caffe2+Eigen 1310 ms (12.84x); ResNet-50 3.88x and 2.29x; MobileNet 4.03x and 2.65x. The wiki's Speedup column also lists GoogleNet at 13.7x (Caffe+OpenBLAS) and 4.45x (Caffe2+Eigen), but its own timing tables give 822/125 = about 6.6x and 267/125 = about 2.1x (derived from page data). VGG-16 on iPhone 7, 2 cores: 284 ms vs TensorFlow Lite 905 ms in the 2-core column, about 3.2x (derived from page data). Nvidia TX2 VGG-16: 706 ms (2 cores) vs Caffe2+NNPACK 3569 ms (about 5x, derived from page data).
corrections.hardware: Samsung S8 (Snapdragon 835), iPhone 7 (A10), Huawei D05 (2x Hi1616, 64 Cortex-A72), Phytium FT1500A/16, RK3399, Raspberry Pi 3B, Nvidia TX2
corrections.caveats: First-party wiki numbers; the D05 section says the tests finished at the end of 2017 and 'performance may change a lot after that time'. No benchmark code is linked and compiler and flags are not stated. The wiki's Speedup column does not match its own tables: GoogleNet is overstated (13.7x listed vs about 6.6x derived; 4.45x vs about 2.1x), while SqueezeNet and DenseNet are understated. There is no top-level LICENSE file (the README badge links a 404), but the source files carry BSD-3-Clause headers (Copyright 2019 THL A29 Limited / Tencent), including the bundled ncnn code. Baselines are Caffe2+Eigen, Caffe+OpenBLAS, TFLite and ACL as of late 2017.

notes: Metadata: 1.2k stars, 275 forks, 19 commits on master, last commit 2019-09-24, not archived; abandoned is correct. Search snippets (paper not opened) say the TPDS 31(3):580-594 abstract reports VGG-16 on a 64-core ARM server 48x/14x/12x faster than Caffe+OpenBLAS/Caffe2+Eigen/NNPACK and 3.19x faster than TFLite on iPhone 7 plus. Candidate for a retier check to B. Shortcoming to record: the wiki's speedup column is internally inconsistent (GoogleNet overstated about 2x).
